//: Two families of cross-user query live in this app, and both need help.
1. The leaderboard, which sorts across users. Every one of its four
windows needs its own composite index: Firestore cannot combine an
equality filter with an ordering on a different field without one. The
`hidden` filter is what keeps an opted-out matchmaker off the board, and
the period key is what keeps last week's numbers out of this week's — so
both are part of every index. The all-time board has no period key, so
it needs one fewer field.
Two `isGreaterThan` filters run against these same indexes and need no
further index of their own, because a range on the field already being
ordered by is free: the `> 0` that keeps a member who published a zero
counter this morning off the board, and the `> myPoints` that counts the
rows above the reader to find their rank.
2. The community totals, which are `sum()` / `count()` aggregates over the
same collection *without* the `hidden` filter — a hidden matchmaker's
work still counts towards what the community did, only their name does
not appear. They carry `periodKey == … && periodActions > 0`, which is
what makes 'שדכנים פעילים' mean 'did at least one thing' rather than
'opened the app'. An equality and a range on two different fields needs
its own index; the all-time version filters on one field only and runs
on the automatic single-field index.
3. The mazel-tov postbox, drained oldest-first by the one person a message
is addressed to: `toUid == me` ordered by `createdAt`. An equality and
an ordering on two different fields, so it needs its own index like
everything else here.
4. The two tip queries, `status == … ` ordered by `createdAt`. Two indexes
for one pair of fields, because the direction is part of a composite
index and the two queries want opposite ones: the approval queue is
read oldest-first, because it is a queue and whoever waited longest is
answered first, and the approved rotation is read newest-first.
They exist because both queries used to run unordered under a `limit`,
which returns documents in document-id order — and these ids are
random. Past the limit the console was showing an arbitrary subset, and
a pending tip outside it would never have been reviewed at all. The
report console has the same fix but needs no index here: it orders by
`createdAt` with no filter beside it, which the automatic single-field
index already serves.
The `*Actions` fields hold weighted activity points now, not a count of
actions. The names were left alone deliberately: renaming them would have
meant rebuilding all four leaderboard indexes and a window in which every
board in the wild returned nothing.
Deploy with: firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes
